paper.title: Thompson Sampling for Learning in Zero-Sum Games

settings.name_in_paper: Unknown two-player zero-sum matrix game with Gaussian bandit feedback, centralized self-play (unique Nash equilibrium)
unmapped: Two-player zero-sum m x n matrix game; a single centralized learner picks mixed strategies x_t, y_t for both players and observes the noisy payoff of the sampled entry (I_t,J_t)
Performance measure is the cumulative duality (Nash) gap sum_t Gap_{A*}(x_t,y_t), not standard regret
Payoff matrix A* assumed to have a unique Nash equilibrium
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t=1,\ldots,T$, the learner chooses both $x_t\in\simplex_m$ and $y_t\in\simplex_n$ ... The learner observes the selected action pair $(I_t,J_t)$ and receives only its noisy payoff $Y_t=A^\star_{I_tJ_t}+\xi_t$, $\xi_t\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)$, where the noise variance $\sigma^2>0$ is known. ... $\mathcal R_T(A):=\sum_{t=1}^T \Gap_A(x_t,y_t)$.

settings.name_in_paper: Zero-sum matrix game with Gaussian bandit feedback, bounded payoffs [-R,R], fully mixed unique equilibrium (lower bound)
unmapped: Two-player zero-sum m x m matrix game, centralized learner, cumulative duality gap
Payoff entries in [-R,R], R known to the policy; policy may depend on (m,R,sigma,T)
settings.definition_quote: Fix a payoff radius $R>0$ and suppose that $m=n\ge4$. Consider any possibly randomized, nonanticipating policy $\pi$ ... The policy may depend on $(m,R,\sigma,T)$ but not on the unknown payoff matrix.

settings.name_in_paper: Separable zero-sum matrix game with unique pure equilibrium, Gaussian bandit feedback (lower bound)
unmapped: Two-player zero-sum matrix game, centralized learner, cumulative duality gap
Separable payoff A*_{ij}=u_i+v_j with unique pure equilibrium (e_1,e_1)
settings.definition_quote: Fix a separable matrix $A^\star$ with $A^\star_{ij}=u_i+v_j$, where $u_1>u_i$ for every $i>1$ and $v_1<v_j$ for every $j>1$. Then, $(e_1,e_1)$ is the unique Nash equilibrium.

symbols.C_mix: instance constant depending on (A*,sigma,m,n); zero for pure equilibria; O(d sqrt(log(ed)))
symbols.C_out: instance constant depending on (A*,sigma,m,n); zero for fully mixed equilibria; O(d(m+n-2d)(1+log(mn))^3)

conditions: A* has a unique Nash equilibrium

source.label: thm:unique-rate
source.quote: Suppose that $m,n\ge2$, $T>mn$, and $A^\star$ has a unique Nash equilibrium. Then, there exist finite nonnegative constants $C_{\rm mix},C_{\rm out},C_0$, depending only on $(A^\star,\sigma,m,n)$, such that Nash-TS satisfies $\E[\mathcal R_T]\le C_{\rm mix}\sqrt T+C_{\rm out}\log(eT)+C_0$. Moreover, $C_{\rm mix}=0$ when the unique equilibrium is pure, and $C_{\rm out}=0$ when it is fully mixed.

results.notes: Quantity is the expected cumulative duality gap (sum of both players' dynamic regrets vs best responses); mapped to 'other'. Comparator approximated by best_action_per_round. Pure-equilibrium case gives C_out log(eT)+C_0 (recorded as r2). Nash-TS is anytime.

conditions: A* has a unique pure Nash equilibrium

source.label: thm:unique-rate
source.quote: Moreover, $C_{\rm mix}=0$ when the unique equilibrium is pure, and $C_{\rm out}=0$ when it is fully mixed.

results.notes: Special case of Theorem 5.1 with C_mix=0, giving O(log T).

symbols.Lambda_core: E[max_j (x*)^T W e_j - min_i e_i^T W y*] with W_ij ~ N(0, 2 sigma^2/(x*_i y*_j)) on the equilibrium supports; 0 iff equilibrium pure

conditions: A* has a unique Nash equilibrium

source.label: thm:exact-core-asymptotics
source.quote: Suppose that $m,n\ge2$ and $A^\star$ has a unique Nash equilibrium. Then, Nash-TS satisfies $\lim_{T\to\infty}\frac{\E[\mathcal R_T]}{\sqrt T}=2\Lambda_{\rm core}$. Moreover, $\Lambda_{\rm core}=0$ when the unique Nash equilibrium is pure, whereas $\Lambda_{\rm core}>0$ otherwise.

results.notes: Exact limit (both upper and lower for Nash-TS); recorded as limsup upper. Implies Theta(sqrt T) for non-pure unique equilibria.

conditions: A* has a unique non-pure Nash equilibrium

source.label: cor:core-coefficient-bound
source.quote: Under the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:exact-core-asymptotics}, when the unique Nash equilibrium is not pure, $\Lambda_{\rm core}\le 2\sigma\sqrt{\log d}[(\min_{j\in J^\star}y_j^\star)^{-1/2}+(\min_{i\in I^\star}x_i^\star)^{-1/2}]$. Moreover, if the equilibrium is uniform on its supports ... $\frac{3\sqrt2}{8}\sigma\sqrt{d\log d}\le\Lambda_{\rm core}\le4\sigma\sqrt{d\log d}$.

results.notes: Bound on the leading coefficient Lambda_core (the limit of E[R_T]/sqrt(T) is 2*Lambda_core), not directly on regret; quantity 'other'. Uniform-on-support case recorded separately.

bound.regime: equilibrium uniform on its supports, x*_i=y*_j=1/d

conditions: A* has a unique non-pure Nash equilibrium uniform on its supports

source.label: cor:core-coefficient-bound
source.quote: $\Lambda_{\rm core}=2\sigma\sqrt{2d}\,\E[\max_{1\le k\le d}G_k]$ ... and $\frac{3\sqrt2}{8}\sigma\sqrt{d\log d}\le\Lambda_{\rm core}\le4\sigma\sqrt{d\log d}$.

results.notes: Upper bound on Lambda_core; the matching lower bound (3*sqrt(2)/8) sigma sqrt(d log d) is recorded as r6.

bound.regime: equilibrium uniform on its supports, x*_i=y*_j=1/d

conditions: A* has a unique non-pure Nash equilibrium uniform on its supports
results.notes: Lower bound on the leading coefficient of Nash-TS specifically (not an algorithm-independent lower bound); algorithm_class 'other' = Nash-TS.

symbols.m: number of actions per player (m=n); NOT combinatorial size

conditions: hard instance has a unique fully mixed Nash equilibrium and entries in [-R,R]

source.label: thm:unique-minimax-lower
source.quote: For every policy $\pi$ described above and every $T\ge1$, there exists a matrix $A_{\pi,T}\in[-R,R]^{m\times m}$ with a unique fully mixed Nash equilibrium such that $\E_{A_{\pi,T}}^\pi[\mathcal R_T(A_{\pi,T})]\ge\frac1{8192}\min\{\frac{RT}{m},\sigma\sqrt{mT\log m}\}$.

results.notes: Expected cumulative duality gap lower bound; quantity 'other'.

conditions: policy uniformly efficient on A* and on separable alternatives replacing one u_i by u_1+eps or one v_j by v_1-eps

source.label: thm:pure-separable-lower
source.quote: Every policy $\pi$ described above satisfies $\liminf_{T\to\infty}\frac{\E_{A^\star}^\pi[\mathcal R_T(A^\star)]}{\log T}\ge2\sigma^2(\sum_{i=2}^m\frac1{u_1-u_i}+\sum_{j=2}^n\frac1{v_j-v_1})$.

results.notes: Uniform efficiency: E[R_T]=o(T^alpha) for all alpha>0 on the family. Gaussian change-of-measure (Lai-Robbins style).
